issues.t: Timing chain tensioner failure
issues.sym: A loud rattle from the engine for a few seconds after a cold start, a check engine light, rough running, or an engine that cranks but will not start. If the chain jumps, the engine can be badly damaged.
issues.why: The early 2.0T engine used a timing chain tensioner that can lose pressure and let the chain go slack. A slack chain can skip a tooth, and because this is an interference engine the valves can then hit the pistons. VW issued service bulletins and a 10-year/100,000-mile warranty extension (VWP-18-07) for these years.
issues.next: Do not ignore a cold-start rattle. Have a shop check the chain stretch and tensioner soon; replacing the tensioner before it fails can prevent a damaged engine. The VW extension has likely ended on most cars, but ask a dealer with your VIN.

issues.t: Intake manifold flap failure
issues.sym: Check engine light (often code P2015), rough idle, hesitation or reduced power. Some owners report the light coming back after a repair.
issues.why: The intake manifold has internal flaps moved by a small arm and motor. The arm, flap shafts or position sensor wear out or break, and the engine computer flags a fault. The usual fix is a new manifold.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A P2015 code almost always means the intake manifold needs replacing; it is not an emergency, but fuel economy and smoothness suffer until it is fixed.

issues.t: Water pump leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the engine, a sweet smell, a low-coolant warning, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The plastic water pump and thermostat housing on this engine can warp and crack. VW issued service bulletins and a limited warranty extension (VWP-19-08) for the water pump on these engines.
issues.next: Check the coolant level and look for pink or purple crust near the pump. Stop driving if the engine overheats. Replace the pump and housing with the updated part, and ask a VW dealer whether any extended coverage still applies.

issues.t: Ignition coil failure and misfires
issues.sym: Shaking at idle, stumbling or loss of power when accelerating, and a flashing check engine light. Misfire codes like P0302 or P0304 are common.
issues.why: The pencil-type ignition coils on these engines wear out, and one bad coil often follows another. Worn spark plugs speed up coil failure.
issues.next: A flashing check engine light means stop driving hard, since unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter. Replace the failed coil, and consider replacing all coils and plugs together if they are original.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves
issues.sym: Rough or uneven idle, hesitation at light throttle, misfires when cold, and slowly worsening fuel economy, usually after 50,000 miles or more.
issues.why: Both CC engines use direct injection, so fuel never washes over the intake valves. Oil vapor from the crankcase bakes onto them and forms carbon deposits that disturb airflow.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm with a scope or misfire data. The fix is a walnut-blast or manual cleaning of the intake valves; keeping up with oil changes and fixing a bad PCV valve slows the buildup.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, a check engine light, hard starting after the car sits, or a low fuel pressure code such as P0087.
issues.why: The engine-driven high-pressure fuel pump and its cam follower can wear, and the pump can stop making enough pressure. VW issued several bulletins on diagnosing the pump and on no-starts after long parking.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure checked with a scan tool. If the pump is weak, replace it and inspect the cam follower it rides on, because a worn follower can damage the camshaft.

issues.t: Fuel pump control module can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or bogs down, often at low speed or when stopping, and may not restart.
issues.why: Power to the fuel pump control module can be interrupted, which stops the fuel pump. VW recalled these cars under NHTSA campaign 17V-509.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the fuel pump control module free of charge.

issues.t: PCV valve failure and oil leaks
issues.sym: A whistling or howling noise from the engine, rough idle, lean codes, oil leaks, or a rear main seal that starts leaking.
issues.why: The crankcase breather (PCV) valve on top of the engine has a diaphragm that tears. Crankcase pressure then builds up and can push oil past seals, including the rear main seal.
issues.next: If you hear a whistle at idle or see new oil leaks, have the PCV valve checked first. It is a simple part, and replacing it early protects the seals.

issues.t: Rear main seal oil leak
issues.sym: Oil drips where the engine meets the transmission, oil spots under the car, and the oil level dropping between changes.
issues.why: The rear crankshaft seal hardens and leaks, and a failed PCV valve can blow it out. Replacing it means removing the transmission, so it is a big job.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and have the source confirmed. Fix the PCV valve at the same time. Manual-transmission cars often do the clutch while the transmission is out.

issues.t: Fuel injector failure
issues.sym: Misfire on one cylinder, rough running, fuel smell, or an injector stuck open that floods the cylinder and makes starting hard.
issues.why: Direct injectors on this engine can stick or leak, and their seals can be pinched during service.
issues.next: Have a shop run injector tests. Replace failed injectors with new seals; a stuck-open injector should be fixed right away because it can wash oil off the cylinder wall.

issues.t: Turbo diverter valve or wastegate rattle
issues.sym: Loss of boost, a whistle or fluttering sound when lifting off the gas, or a rattle from the turbo above about 2,500 rpm.
issues.why: The turbo diverter (blow-off) valve diaphragm can tear, and the wastegate linkage can wear and rattle. VW issued a bulletin with a clip for the wastegate rod.
issues.next: A torn diverter valve is a simple part. For a wastegate rattle, ask a dealer about the service bulletin fix before replacing the turbo.

issues.t: Throttle body or wiring fault causes EPC light
issues.sym: The EPC and check engine lights come on and the car goes into limp mode with very little power.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body or the wiring harness to it can fail or lose contact. VW issued a bulletin to re-pin the connector on some cars.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A shop may only need to repair the connector; if the throttle body itself has failed, it is replaced.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump oil leak
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the back of the engine near the cylinder head, burning oil smell, and in rare cases a firm brake pedal.
issues.why: The engine-driven vacuum pump that helps the brake booster has seals that leak oil as they age.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Resealing or replacing the vacuum pump fixes it; if the brake pedal feels hard, get it checked right away.

issues.t: DSG transmission shudder or erratic shifting
issues.sym: Shudder or jerking when pulling away, harsh or delayed shifts at low speed, a flashing gear display, or limp mode.
issues.why: The DSG dual-clutch transmission needs fluid changes about every 40,000 miles. Worn clutches or a failing mechatronic control unit cause shudder and shift faults.
issues.next: Have the DSG fluid and filter changed if it is due, then have the clutch and mechatronic adapted with a scan tool. If faults continue, a clutch pack or mechatronic unit may be needed.

issues.t: Takata driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The risk is only in a crash that deploys the driver airbag.
issues.why: The Takata driver airbag inflator can build up too much pressure and burst, throwing metal pieces at the driver. Covered by NHTSA campaigns 16V-078 and 18V-148.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the inflator replaced as soon as possible. The repair is free.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture on 2015-2017 models (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The risk is only in a crash that deploys the driver airbag.
issues.why: The driver frontal airbag inflator can over-pressurize and burst when it deploys. VW recalled these cars under NHTSA campaign 19V-014.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer replace the inflator for free.

issues.t: Clock spring damage can disable the driver airbag (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, and the horn or steering wheel buttons may stop working.
issues.why: Debris can tear the clock spring cable inside the steering column, cutting power to the driver airbag. VW recalled these cars under NHTSA campaign 15V-483.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer installs a protective cover or a new clock spring for free.

issues.t: Airbag control unit can fail (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: A capacitor in the airbag control unit can fail, so airbags may not deploy in a crash or may deploy without one. VW recalled these cars under NHTSA campaign 19V-535.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the software and replaces the control unit if needed, free of charge.

issues.t: Wrong front head restraints may be fitted (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you will notice in daily driving.
issues.why: Some cars were built with the wrong front head restraints, which may not protect your head properly in a rear crash. VW recalled them under NHTSA campaign 17V-287.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the head restraints free of charge.

issues.t: Rear child locks can switch off (recall)
issues.sym: A rear door that should be child-locked can be opened from inside.
issues.why: Vibration can make the rear child lock disengage. VW recalled these cars under NHTSA campaign 16V-464.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer inspects and replaces the child locks if needed, free of charge.

issues.t: Passenger seat belt wiring can switch off the airbag (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light may come on with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The wiring to the passenger seat belt buckle was routed where it can be damaged, which can switch off the passenger front airbag. VW recalled these cars under NHTSA campaign 09V-097.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer reroutes the wiring and replaces it if damaged, free of charge.

issues.t: Port-installed wheels may lack proper tire pressure sensors (recall)
issues.sym: The tire pressure warning light may stay on or may not warn you about a low tire.
issues.why: Some accessory wheels and tires fitted at the port did not have the correct tire pressure sensors. VW recalled these cars under NHTSA campaign 11V-312.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. VW replaces the sensors free of charge.

issues.t: Cupped or uneven front tire wear
issues.sym: A humming or droning noise that gets louder with speed, vibration, and front tires wearing in scalloped patches or on the inside edge.
issues.why: Owners and RepairPal report tire cupping on the CC. Worn struts, alignment that is out of spec and skipped tire rotations make it worse.
issues.next: Rotate the tires regularly and have the alignment and struts checked. Replace badly cupped tires, since the noise will not go away on its own.

issues.t: Worn struts and strut mounts
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, a bouncy or floaty ride, or a creak when turning the wheel at low speed.
issues.why: Struts and their upper mounts and bearings wear out with mileage and are among the more commonly replaced parts on the CC.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected. Replace struts in pairs along with their mounts, and get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Headlight and tail light bulb failures
issues.sym: A bulb-out warning on the dash, or a headlight, brake light or turn signal that does not light.
issues.why: Headlight bulbs are one of the most-replaced parts on the CC in owner surveys. Cars with xenon lights can also have a failing igniter or ballast.
issues.next: Replace the bulb in pairs. If a xenon headlight flickers or stays out with a new bulb, have the ballast checked.

issues.t: Radio and navigation unit freezes or fails
issues.sym: The touchscreen freezes, reboots, goes blank or loses navigation, radio or Bluetooth.
issues.why: The factory radio and navigation head units can fail, sometimes after a software update.
issues.next: Try a full reset by turning the car off and opening the driver door for a few minutes. If it keeps failing, a software update or a replacement unit is needed.

issues.t: Exterior trim and roof molding coming loose
issues.sym: Chrome or black trim strips along the roof or doors peel, lift, flap at speed or come off.
issues.why: The adhesive on the roof and side moldings weakens with heat and age; trim is a frequently reported repair in owner surveys.
issues.next: Have loose trim reattached or replaced before it blows off on the highway.
